facts.fact: The decree of 2 October 2019 keeps the paper register as the legal record: acts are drawn up in registers of fifty-leaf volumes printed by the Imprimerie nationale and kept in duplicate, and where a computerised act and the paper differ the physical form prevails (arts 8, 9, 24).

The decree permits, without requiring, civil status acts to be established by computerised processes in addition to manual ones, through an automated processing hosted by the commune or sous-préfecture and used to establish acts, transcribe court decisions and add marginal mentions; under shared use each office sees only the acts it holds (arts 24, 25, 28).
facts.system: traitement automatisé des données de l'état civil

facts.fact: The decree's permission to establish acts by computerised processes covers civil status acts in general, births and deaths among them, with marriages; it states a permission in law and gives no count of offices using it (arts 24, 25).
facts.system: traitement automatisé des données de l'état civil

facts.fact: The decree places the automated processing with the commune or sous-préfecture itself, subject to prior authorisation by the national personal-data protection authority and conformity checks by the public prosecutor; hosting may be delegated to a public body or, exceptionally, to a private one established and hosting in Côte d'Ivoire (arts 25, 26, 34).
